CurrentLocation: Israel Museum, Jerusalem, and other museums
Description: More than two thousand jar handles stamped before firing with the Hebrew letters lmlk — 'belonging to the king' — plus one of four towns (Hebron, Ziph, Socoh, or mmst) and a winged scarab or sun disk. First found by Charles Warren in 1869, they cluster in Judah and date to the reign of Hezekiah, most likely a royal stockpiling program ahead of Sennacherib's invasion in 701 BC.
BiblicalSignificance: When Assyria marched on Judah, Hezekiah did not only pray — he prepared: storehouses, waterworks, and stamped jars of oil, wine, and grain ready for a siege. The lmlk seals are the logistics of faith under pressure, the same king who spread Sennacherib's letter before the LORD also making sure the jars were full.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the stamps are genuine royal Judahite jar marks; debate concerns the meaning of ‘mmst’ (a place or the government) and whether the system was Hezekiah’s alone.
